h: Planning your night in the capital
p: Golf Fang is strictly 18+, so this is an adults' night out from start to finish. The best evenings tend to have a loose plan: a tee time booked, a rough idea of where you'll eat, and a list of bars to try afterwards. Cardiff's city centre is compact, so once the golf's done you can walk to most places in minutes.

Some easy wins for a good round. Settle the teams and any forfeits early, be fair about whose turn it is, and remember that laughing at someone's fourth attempt at the loop-the-loop is basically compulsory. If you're celebrating, tell the team when you book; venues like this often have options for bigger groups, and it saves a scramble on the night.

Make a weekend of it and Cardiff has loads to offer. By day, Cardiff Castle sits right in the heart of the city with its Roman walls, Norman keep and lavish Victorian rooms, and the Principality Stadium looms over the river nearby. The Victorian Cardiff Market and the city's historic arcades are packed with independent shops and food stalls, and Cardiff Bay has the Wales Millennium Centre and a lovely waterfront walk. On big match or concert days the city fills up fast, so if your visit lines up with one, book your golf and your table well in advance and expect busy streets.
